channel.title: The Price of Germany
channel.description: Videos, guides and cost breakdowns about life and money in Germany.

item.title: Nobody Is Showing You What the EU Actually Paid Disinfo Lab (4 Projects, 8 Years)
item.description: A headline says Europe is spending taxpayer billions to brand America a disinformation threat. I followed the money in the EU's own grant database. A German taxpayer's share works out to about a third of a cent.

item.title: Why German Gas Is Still 2.1x More Expensive Than The US
item.description: Lars fills his tank in Leipzig for $123; Kyle fills the same in Cincinnati for about $58. Germany just cut fuel tax again, and gas still costs 2.1x more. I opened up a liter and counted every cent, and the yearly bill is the twist.

item.title: Can You Actually Survive on Minimum Wage in Germany?
item.description: Same age, same hours, same job at the minimum wage. Jana in Dortmund ends the month with 550 euros left over; Tyler outside Jackson ends $225 short. I rebuilt both months line by line.

item.title: The $19,000 Baby Bill Nobody Warns Americans About (Germany Pays $0)
item.description: Two babies born the same night, 4,800 miles apart. Anna in Munich paid $0. Sarah in Florida got a $19,000 bill, with good insurance. Here is the entire first year, line by line.

item.title: The Hidden Bill Behind Germany's Chancellor Crisis
item.description: Merz failed his own confidence vote, cratered to 9% approval, and got wiped out in three state elections. A Leipzig machinist and a Cincinnati car buyer never met, and both are paying for it. Here is the real bill.

item.title: Inside Berlin's €36 Billion Plan to Seize 240,000 Apartments
item.description: Berlin made a party that wants to convert nearly 240,000 corporate apartments into public housing its strongest since reunification. Two neighbors read the same 25.7% headline and had opposite mornings. Here is the real bill: 8 to 36 billion euros.

item.title: How a US Missile Deal Ends Up on a German Teacher's Tax Bill
item.description: Dana builds Tomahawk parts in Arkansas; her overtime beats her mortgage. Jonas teaches in Dresden under a two-year leaking ceiling. A US-Germany missile deal quietly attached both their lives, and the ~108 billion euro bill lands on taxpayers who never voted on it.

item.title: How a Heating Bill Is Driving Germany's Far-Right Surge (Not Immigration)
item.description: Two neighbors one wall apart in Halle, same age and same bills, opposite votes. What best predicted the difference was not ideology, it was heat, rent, and pensions. The cost story under the AfD surge.

item.title: The Real Reason Germany Voted AfD (America Already Did It)
item.description: Everyone called Germany's 43.8% AfD result a far-right immigration earthquake. The people who studied the vote say it was cost of living, and it already happened in America. Petra in Halle and Mike near Youngstown made the same choice for the same reason.

item.title: Inside Germany's Real East vs West Divide (It's Not Income)
item.description: Mara in Chemnitz and Paul near Munich, same graduating class, nearly the same salary. 36 years after reunification they live completely different financial lives, and the reason is not the paycheck.

item.title: The True Cost of Raising a Kid: Germany vs the US (18 Years)
item.description: Two babies born the same week, one in Germany, one in Ohio. By 18, their parents will have spent wildly different amounts. Here is the real 18-year ledger, category by category.

item.title: How a €3,000 Drone Cost Germany Billions, And Who Really Pays
item.description: A €3,000 drone crashed near Leipzig's airport in August 2026. It never even went off. It still cost two countries consulates, diplomats, and billions of euros. Here is the real bill, and who quietly pays it.

item.title: Germany Might Force Freelancers Into Pensions, America Already Did
item.description: Lukas in Leipzig and Danielle in Austin both think they handle their own retirement. Only one is right. Germany is debating forcing freelancers to pay in; the US already does, with zero opt-out.

item.title: Laid Off in Germany vs the US: What Nobody Tells Americans
item.description: Dana in Mississippi and Lukas near Dortmund get laid off the same week. A year later their bank accounts look nothing alike, and in some US states the laid-off worker out-earns the German.

item.title: Why Germans Don't Invest and Still Retire Just Fine
item.description: Only 1 in 6 Germans own stocks, and Jana in Leipzig still parks her money in a savings account earning next to nothing. So why is she not broke? The real answer is stranger than the myth.

item.title: Inside Germany's €10 Billion "Tax Cut" (It's Not Free Money)
item.description: Germany announced a €10 billion tax cut, and Mara in Berlin and Kyle in Ohio both got a bit richer without knowing why. Open the number up and it is barely a tax cut at all.

item.title: The End of 'Made in Germany'? Why the Economic Engine is Breaking
item.description: Everyone still thinks German industry is unstoppable. Markus just found a layoff notice on the breakroom door. 272,000 industrial jobs gone since 2019, and the pain lands nothing like it would in the US.

item.title: What an AfD Win Really Costs Germany
item.description: Torsten votes out of frustration. Andrea's US client already paused a contract over the same election. Same city, two very different bills, and a political cost nobody puts on a postcard.

item.title: Germany Paid Her €1,200 a Month. America Paid Her $0.
item.description: Same job title, same salary, due dates 11 days apart. Megan came home to $0. Julia came home to two-thirds of her paycheck, automatically, for over a year.

item.title: Why German Electricity Costs 2x the US (It's Not the Solar Panels)
item.description: Kevin in Phoenix pays $187 and shrugs. Lena in Leipzig watches her bill climb without touching the thermostat. Here is where German electricity money really goes.

item.title: I Paid $50 to Charge My EV in Germany. My Friend Paid $11 in Texas.
item.description: Mike charged his Tesla near Austin for $11. I charged a comparable amount off the Autobahn and paid nearly $50. Same car, wildly different bill.

item.title: Why Peptides Cost Up to 20x More in the USA Than Germany (Wegovy, Zepbound & BPC-157)
item.description: The same peptide can cost $1,297 in the USA and 61 euros in Germany. Same ingredient, wildly different price. Here is exactly why.

item.title: The REAL Cost of Owning a Car in Germany vs the USA
item.description: Gas costs over $9 a gallon in Germany, so owning a car must cost a fortune, right? Not even close.

item.title: Is Germany Cheaper Than America? The Honest Numbers
item.description: Two new dads, two very different bills. Where Germany quietly saves you tens of thousands, and where it will make your eyes water.

item.title: Study in Germany vs. USA: Is the Debt Worth It?
item.description: Everyone says German uni is free. The real numbers: semester fees, health insurance, the blocked account, and the one catch that isn't money at all.

item.title: The German Salary Trap: Why Your Gross Pay Is A Lie
item.description: A real €75,000 payslip broken down line by line, and why Mike's 53% take-home isn't as far behind Sarah's 77% in Texas as it looks.

item.title: The Emotional Tax of Living in Germany
item.description: What German directness actually costs in chronic stress and strained relationships, and the €0 fix that's been sitting there the whole time.

item.title: "Free" Daycare in Germany? The Real Cost, State by State
item.description: Sarah in Austin pays $420 every two weeks. Lukas in Berlin pays €23 a month. What parents actually pay across all 16 German states.

item.title: What Moving to Germany Actually Costs: $8,000 vs. $19,000
item.description: The real line-by-line breakdown: blocked account, health insurance, shipping, deposits, and the hidden setup costs nobody budgets for.

item.title: This Cheap German Insurance Could Save You From Bankruptcy
item.description: Why personal liability insurance costs 50 to 80 euros a year in Germany and covers up to 50 million euros, versus a $100,000 renter's policy in the US.
